text: The room Straker left that night
why: ¶82 says Straker picked up the knife 'as he left the room', and ¶32 says he dressed and then left the house that night, so this room is the one he left.
¶82 names the dressing-table, where the knife had lain before Straker picked it up.

text: The disk of cork that guarded the knife's tip
why: ¶82 states the knife's tip was guarded by a cork disk found beside the body.

text: When Mrs. Straker told the Inspector of the knife
why: ¶82 reports that Mrs. Straker told the Inspector about the knife's location. The story gives no exact time, but the telling clearly happened before the present conversation.

text: What Inspector Gregory reports at the house
why: ¶82 is the Inspector reporting the knife, the cork disk and the wife's account at the house, where the conversation takes place.

text: What Mrs. Straker told the Inspector
why: ¶82 states that Mrs. Straker told the Inspector the knife had lain on the dressing-table and that Straker picked it up as he left the room.
